question: A can lay railway track between two given stations in 17 days and B can do the same job in 16 days. With the help of C, they did the job in 4 days only. Then, C alone can do the job in
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(17, 16, 4) = 272 units.

Efficiency of A = 272 ÷ 17 = 16 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 272 ÷ 16 = 17 units/day.

Efficiency of A, B, and C together = 272 ÷ 4 = 68 units/day.

Efficiency of C = 68 − (16 + 17) = 35 units/day.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 ²⁷⁄₃₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 17 days.

Time taken by B = 16 days.

Time taken by A, B, and C together = 4 days.

**Method Used:**

We use the LCM method to find the total work and the efficiency of each person.

Total Work = LCM of days taken by given persons or groups.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days.

 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of C = Combined Efficiency of (A + B + C) − (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 68 − (16 + 17)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 68 − 33 = 35 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 272 ÷ 35

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 7 ²⁷⁄₃₅ days

**∴ The correct answer is 7 ²⁷⁄₃₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Concepts are similar to Time and Work. Fill pipes have positive efficiency (adding work), and empty pipes have negative efficiency (removing work).

Work and Wages

Total wages are distributed in direct proportion to the actual amount of work done by each individual. If they work for an equal number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

If persons work on alternate days, you group the work into cycles (e.g., A works on Day 1, B works on Day 2 → 1 cycle = 2 days). Find the combined work done in one cycle and scale it up to reach close to the total work.
